text:
1	# Prelude architecture
2	
3	Prelude is a tool for designing and then building an app with an agent: you pick a project, chat with the Claude Code CLI, and watch the design appear beside the chat. It runs as one Node server (plain `node:http`, views in Eta, Koda in the page) on localhost:4200, optionally inside a Tauri desktop window. Everything it produces is files in the project's `prelude/` folder, each design worked on in its own git branch and worktree. Agent-written views render in a sandboxed child process, and each design is served on its own preview origin.
4	
5	## Layers
6	
7	1. Windows
8	2. Entry points
9	3. Pages
10	4. Agent and live state
11	5. Designs and hosting
12	6. Project files
13	7. Shared helpers
14	8. Outside
15	
16	## Principles
17	
18	- **The folder is the database.** Everything Prelude makes is a file under the project's `prelude/`, committed with the code; `~/.prelude/` holds only machine-local conveniences, so nothing is lost if it's deleted.
19	- **The server is the single source of truth for live state.** Every window (chat, pop-out, browser tab) renders from the server and re-renders on its SSE events, so no window holds state another needs.
20	- **Agent-written code never runs in the server's process.** A design's views render in a sandboxed renderer, and a host that runs them unsandboxed starts only once the person approves it.
21	- **The agent works with ordinary file tools, fenced to what it may touch.** It reads the project and the folders added as references, writes only where its mode allows, and deletes by writing a file empty.
22	- **A design's memory is its files, not a conversation.** Each session starts from NOTES.md, the views and states, so sessions on different machines and branches pick up where the work stands.
23	- **Committed files must merge cleanly.** Session folders and decision ids are random, transcripts are append-only, and there's no shared index that every session rewrites.

1	# Rules: Design Workspace
2	
3	- **R-7vq.** A window’s size and client are its own: the pop-out can show a phone in the mobile app while the surface beside the chat fits the panel, and changing one never changes the other.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*
5	- **R-c2m.** The page and the state on show belong to the design, so picking either moves every window showing it.
6	- **R-h9x.** Every design in a project offers the same sizes and clients: the ones its app shell declares, with Fit the panel always first.
7	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design @ typical*
8	- **R-e5n.** A custom size takes a width and a height between 200 and 4000 pixels; anything outside that shows the page fitting the panel.
9	- **R-w3j.** A design remembers one custom size, offered in every window’s size menu after the shell’s sizes; setting another replaces it.
10	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*
11	- **R-b6d.** A message may be images alone, with no words.
12	- **R-x8f.** The agent sees every image sent with a message, and the images stay with the session, so they’re still there when it’s opened again.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design/window @ popped-out*
14	- **R-m2s.** Only images can be attached (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP); pasting or dropping anything else leaves the message box as it was.
15	- **R-r7h.** Each message tells the agent what the person was looking at when they sent it (the page, the state, and the size and client when they aren’t the defaults), unless they turned that off for it.
16	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design @ typical*
17	- **R-z4k.** Messages sent while the agent is working wait, and go to it together, in the order they were written, when its turn ends.
18	  *shown-on: /f/:folder/d/:design @ agent-working*
19	- **R-9cn.** Stopping the agent sends nothing that was waiting: the waiting messages go back into the message box, to send or change.

1	# Design Workspace - notes
2	
3	A redesign of Prelude's design page (`/f/:folder/d/:design`, its sessions and
4	the pop-out window): today `server/views/_session.eta`, `_design.eta`,
5	`_branch.eta`, `_entry.eta`, `_status.eta`, `_composer.eta`, `_window.eta`.
6	It renders in the shell's `workspace` and `window` layouts. The routes carry
7	`"from": "@app/server/views/…"`, so the build ports it back.
8	
9	Pages: Design page, with drawers (About the design, Rules, Open
10	questions) and modals (an image, Mark up, Turn on dictation); Pop-out
11	window. The fake project is a lender's borrower portal, so sizes (phone,
12	tablet) and a second client (its mobile app) mean something. States:
13	typical, pages differ, doesn't render, agent working, new design, update
14	clashed, popped out, new session; and for visuals in the chat: a flow and
15	a map, several visuals, a visual not drawn, visuals popped out, drawing a
16	visual (streaming), ask and fix (a fix's conversation, its own design).
17	
18	All seven items of the first review are now designed or settled (item 4,
19	the record picker, was dropped).

22	
23	- **Scope: 1-3 of the review, plus the pop-out** (the person, 2026-10-17):

26	  with pills for what to act on (check, behind main, a clash). It opens a
27	  drawer (`/about`) with the branch in full and its actions, what the design
28	  uses, and what the agent can read. An update that clashed also shows as a
29	  notice above the work, since it holds the branch.

3	     (Whisper); no speech service sees it (R-f2y). So it works the same in a
4	     browser and in the desktop app. `it` is the design; `it.dictation` is
5	     the person's set-up, kept for them on this machine, not for the design:
6	       - no model yet: the microphone opens the modal, to choose one and
7	         download it (once);
8	       - downloading: how far it's got, with Cancel; the region holding
9	         this (#dictation, in the composer) reloads as the server says it's
10	         moved on (dictation-changed);
11	       - ready: press to speak; press again to stop. The recording goes to
12	         the server with what's typed so far, and the box comes back with

14	         "Typing what you said…" goes. The server tells the model this

2	     a region of its own (#design-bar, at …/preview/bar). It reloads when the

7	     loads it again (R-v2q). What the person does themselves (a page, a
8	     state, a size) reloads the whole surface at once, in every window.
9
